summary.en: Research on quantum theory, gravitation, spacetime, and quantum information.

papers.title: Observer-Separated Two-Time Quantum Dynamics
papers.subtitle: Local Horizon Obstructions, Cross-Perspective Consistency, and Finite-Dimensional Evaporation Bounds
papers.author: Yohtaro Soga

summary.en: An observer-indexed quantum framework separates reversible clock-time evolution from auxiliary-time dephasing, with conditional results on energy conservation, local horizon incompatibility, quantum recovery, entropy, and information bottlenecks.

general.en: Explore horizons, observer records, two kinds of quantum evolution, and information recovery through examples.

student.en: Work through matrix generators, energy variance, a Hawking pair, channel fidelity, pinching, and evaporation models.

expert.en: Read the assumptions, conditional theorem statements, mathematical constructions, and the limits of the finite models.

en: All guides cover the two-time framework, the five conditional results, the two-window evaporation example, the independent matrix-spectrum benchmark, and open questions.

The mathematical statements concern specified finite-dimensional systems. No continuum gravitational dephasing, observed firewall, or experimentally measured departure from standard quantum mechanics is asserted.

papers.title: Consistency Audits of Observer-Separated Open Dynamics in 2D Dilaton Gravity
papers.subtitle: KMS Covariance, Non-Gaussian JT Fluctuations, and Chiral-Horizon Obstructions
papers.author: Yohtaro Soga

summary.en: The continuation of OSTQD extends its finite-dimensional framework to thermal open systems and conditional low-energy gravity models. It derives frozen-coefficient JT fluctuation cumulants and a smooth-band chiral-horizon obstruction, with separate checks of KMS covariance, greybody scattering and quantum-channel bottlenecks.

general.en: Follow the physical questions behind thermal baths, fluctuating black holes, horizon correlations, and information recovery.

student.en: Work through thermal channel equations, energy cumulants, point-split correlations, and controlled model comparisons.

expert.en: Examine the hypotheses, proof strategies, analytic obstructions, quantitative controls, and formalization boundaries.

en: The paper builds on the preceding finite-dimensional OSTQD study by relaxing strict subsystem energy conservation for reduced open systems. The guides cover SK normalization, KMS covariance and its time-dependent limits, Ward identities and JT fluctuation closures, bosonic and chiral-horizon diagnostics, per-port thermal locking, greybody scattering, and separated information benchmarks.

The focused analytical results are conditional: a specified free chiral-boson smooth-band defect and the frozen-coefficient JT cumulant closure. A positive global continuum state, a microscopic rate, observer-separated outcome instruments and a unified evaporation endpoint remain open.
